newsitem.title: CHINA: China's sole reinsurer expects business boom.
newsitem.headline: China's sole reinsurer expects business boom.

text.p: China's only reinsurer aims for a business turnover jump of 50 percent this year to 10.4 billion yuan ($1.25 billion) as the market booms and demand for life insurance increases, the China Daily said on Sunday.

PICC Reinsurance Co president Dai Fengju told the newspaper the 1997 turnover target was 200 million yuan ($24 million) from commercial premiums and 10.2 billion yuan ($1.23 billion) from reinsurance business assigned by the government.
Under China's insurance laws, domestic insurers must distribute 20 percent of all business except life insurance to PICC Reinsurance in order to diversify their risks.
Dai said property reinsurance formed the bulk of his company's current business, but that life reinsurance was expected to take off as more Chinese take out policies.
The China Daily said about 300 million of China's 1.2 billion people have life insurance, and that annual life insurancee premiums should hit 144 billion yuan by 2000.
PICC Reinsurance planned to offer life reinsurance this year, and is drafting regulations and training personnel to develop the market, the newspaper said.

Established in July 1996, PICC Reinsurance is one of three subsidiaries of the People's Insurance Company (Group) of China, the country's largest insurer. The other two are PICC Life and PICC Property.
